name: repo-review reference corpus
note: The recorded streams are the spike's two-subagent read tasks (#281): repo-review shaped (a lead delegating lookups to two native subagents), not a review of a real pull request. Every case says which part is a real recording and what, if anything, was changed or stood in.

cases.proves: Lead, two native subagents, a Read each, final result; edges observed and hook cross-checked

cases.change: the last child tool_result gets is_error=true
cases.proves: A tool fails, the attempt completes, the graph is unchanged

cases.change: first 40 lines, then the stand-in never finishes
cases.proves: The host's wall-time limit interrupts the attempt

cases.change: first 40 lines, then the stand-in waits for SIGTERM
cases.proves: User cancel: SIGTERM first, attempt cancelled

cases.change: cut after the first child Read tool_use; the process is then killed; the store is torn; a second attempt runs
cases.proves: Interrupted attempt with an open tool, torn-tail repair, new attempt, nothing resumed
Interleaved children and concurrent stderr lose nothing

cases.change: broken JSON, invalid UTF-8, an unknown event type and a cut-off last line are inserted
cases.proves: Damage becomes labelled gaps and warnings, the graph is unchanged

cases.change: usage, cost, durations and turn counts removed
cases.proves: No usage reported stays unknown in the store and every view

cases.change: none; also the compiled plan of fixtures/workflows/graph/repo-review.toml and the argv builder
cases.proves: Denial is vendor auto-deny, never an approval aibus invented; held steps are in the plan; interactive approval is unsupported
Offline replay with an empty PATH, byte for byte repeatable, rerun refused
